branch_activations.independent_trigger: The fronted exclusive object identifies the recipient, and the aid request keeps the act of honoring dependent.
branch_activations.activation: The active worship relation is viewed from its honored endpoint while the speakers seek support for performing it.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Worship is also the speakers' recognition of the addressee's high regard.
branch_activations.boundary: B006 names the recipient's treatment; no active causative sense or increase in intrinsic divine greatness is invented.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu yüksek konumun sonucu olarak kişiye hizmet edilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The respected recipient is served in consequence of being held high.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The exclusive address singles out the one served; help-seeking supplies the speakers' dependence in rendering service.
branch_activations.activation: The source's dignity-to-service relation explains why the speakers' act can magnify its recipient without being self-sufficient.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Honoring is enacted through service whose support is sought.
branch_activations.boundary: This associated facet accompanies F001 and preserves the source's recipient-oriented relation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, topluluk veya şey, başka birinin işini yapmasına destek olur ya da o işte kullanılabilecek bir destek oluşturur.
branch_activations.carrier: Help is backing for an action.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Worship names the service through which the recipient is honored.
branch_activations.activation: The help request meets the honoring action as its sought support.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speakers do not claim their honoring act originates in self-sufficient power.
branch_activations.boundary: The relation is a local inference and does not promise the request's fulfillment.

findings.title: Help imagined as protective attention
findings.claim: The exclusive aid request may be heard as placing the serving community under attentive, preserving care, with their honoring service performed within that attention.
findings.mechanism: The packet's explicit non-dominant mapping links the help carrier at 1:5:4:1 to the protective-watchfulness branch. Honoring service at 1:5:2:1 supplies an independent relational act: sustained regard for the addressee meets a source image in which regard for a person protects them. This contact gives requested aid the exploratory form of preserving attention, while the shared address joins the request to the serving community.
findings.reader_payoff: From aid imagined as intervention or added force, the reader may also perceive sustained watchful presence around the act of service.
findings.containment: The exact HFT watchful-care role, honoring-service role, before/after change, and containment are retained. The QAC root remains the help root; the eye-root link is a supplied non-dominant mapping, not an alternative morphological derivation. Protective attention is an attributed resonance, never the verb's lexical gloss. No anatomical eye, surveillance, harmful gaze, reciprocal obligation, or guarantee of protection is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The trace is legacy_unbound, but its word indices agree with the supplied QAC words and its split-root mapping is explicitly present. The protective-watchfulness branch is independently supplied. Its local application remains attributed because morphology alone does not establish the eye-root resonance.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiyi göz önünde bulundurarak korumayı, kollamayı ve gözetmeyi belirtir.
branch_activations.carrier: Ordinary seeking of aid carries, through the supplied split mapping, an attributed image of protective watchfulness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The honoring act of service and renewed personal address supply the relationship within which care is sought.
branch_activations.activation: The service is an ongoing act before its addressed recipient; the mapped protection image makes help imaginable as keeping that serving group in preserving attention.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Aid may take the imagined shape of attentive care surrounding the service.
branch_activations.boundary: The map permits review but does not prove lexical activation. This is the exact HFT role, qualified as a possibility; QAC still analyzes the help root.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi çevresindekilerce saygıdeğer ve yüce tutulur.
branch_activations.carrier: The service-root's recipient description supplies honor and magnification.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The aid request under the same exclusive address is the separate relation in which protective attention is being explored.
branch_activations.activation: Honoring the addressee identifies the community's relational act, so the watchful-care possibility returns to an actual act performed here.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The attentive-care image surrounds a community actively honoring its addressee.
branch_activations.boundary: The direction of honoring is toward the addressee; protective care is requested toward the speakers. These directions are distinguished, not converted into a contractual reciprocity.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu yüksek konumun sonucu olarak kişiye hizmet edilir.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The separate request seeks aid for the speakers acting in that service relation.
branch_activations.activation: The actual service verb supplies the activity performed under the attributed protective attention.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Watchful presence concerns sustained service, not a detached visual image.
branch_activations.boundary: This associated service facet accompanies the honor core. It does not lexically reparse the active verb as a recipient noun.

findings.title: One addressed You and a shared acting We
findings.claim: Both acts are spoken by a plural We to the same singular You, making dependence as collective as service.
findings.mechanism: First-person plural agreement in 1:5:2:1 and 1:5:4:1 meets second-person singular address in 1:5:1:1 and 1:5:3:2. Repetition preserves this number asymmetry across the change of act: the speaking group serves together and speaks its need together.
findings.reader_payoff: The aid request does not retreat into a private I after the collective declaration; the same shared voice occupies both acts.
findings.containment: Plural morphology establishes the speaking form, not the historical size, identity, institutional boundaries, or internal unanimity of an actual group. A single reciter can utter this supplied plural voice.

epistemic.reason: This is an independently noticed relation among four fully aligned local morphemes, corroborated by the supplied plural-verb and repeated-addressee evidence.

findings.title: Performed service and acknowledged belonging
findings.claim: The plural declaration of worship may also make the speakers' belonging to the addressed divine recipient perceptible as a shared relation expressed through their service.
findings.mechanism: The service root also names a person as belonging to God and, in its plural extension, an affiliated community. The distinct aid-seeking verb addresses the same source with the same plural subject, bringing the act of service into contact with a sustained relation of dependence. Their worship can thus voice an acknowledged belonging, while act and status remain distinct.
findings.reader_payoff: The shared declaration is intelligible as expression of a relationship as well as performance of an act.
findings.containment: The lexical source predicates belonging on createdness and can extend to every person; this local resonance applies only to the speaking group as presented and does not derive a universal doctrine or an exclusive community membership test from the verb. The focus remains an active verb, not the branch's noun for a servant or community. The relation is distinct from legal ownership.

epistemic.reason: This uncandidate branch has supplied lexical facets and a mapped focus carrier. The second plural act and common addressed source provide an independent relation; applying the nominal belonging field to the active declaration is a bounded inference.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: Tanrı'ya ait sayılan insan veya topluluk
branch_activations.facet_statement: Her insan yaratılmışlık ve aitlik bakımından Tanrı'nın kulu sayılabilir.
branch_activations.carrier: Worshipful service has a root-associated nominal relation of a person belonging to God by createdness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The separate active plural help request addresses the same source of dependence.
branch_activations.activation: Performing service and seeking aid from the same addressed recipient makes belonging a possible relational background to the acts.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speakers' service can express acknowledged belonging as well as an undertaken deed.
branch_activations.boundary: Createdness is the lexical source's ground of belonging, not a new independently proven premise about every person from this ayah. Do not turn the active verb into the noun or legal status.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: Tanrı'ya ait sayılan insan veya topluluk
branch_activations.facet_statement: Çoğul adlandırma, Tanrı'ya bağlı topluluğu veya onun tarafında bulunanları gösterebilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The same nominal field can designate an affiliated community.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Plural aid-seeking repeats the plural service subject and the common singular addressee.
branch_activations.activation: Shared dependency makes the plural extension relationally relevant: the We performing service is also the We seeking support from its addressed source.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: A community-shaped belonging becomes audible through the parallel acts.
branch_activations.boundary: This extension accompanies the core belonging facet. It does not identify an institutional group, declare outsiders excluded, or reinterpret verbal agreement as a literal plural noun.
